title: The LATEST audit-verdict row per acceptance criterion is authoritative; earlier rows are audit history, not competing claims
decision: Record explicitly that `audit_record` is APPEND-ONLY and that, where an acceptance criterion carries more than one audit-verdict row, the highest-numbered (most recent) row is the authoritative verdict and every earlier row is retained deliberately as audit history. No earlier row is to be deleted, rewritten, or back-filled to match the current verdict. Consequently, any count that sums audit-verdict ROWS rather than criteria overstates the population: at the time of this decision the package holds 95 verdict rows for 86 criteria, and the 9 extras are supersessions, not disagreements — AC-078 and AC-080 carry three rows each, AC-077, AC-079, AC-083, AC-084 and AC-085 carry two.
rationale: Surfaced by a read-only integrity audit on 2026-08-05, which found seven criteria simultaneously holding a Pending row AND a later Met or Partial row with nothing in the schema marking which governs. The audit-verdict schema has no superseded_by or retired_at column, so the ordering rule cannot be expressed structurally and must be written down or it stays an unstated convention that each reader re-derives. Append-only is the RIGHT behaviour for an audit trail and is not being treated as a defect: it preserves how a verdict evolved, which is exactly what an auditor needs — AC-078 legibly moving Pending to Partial to Met as evidence accumulated is more trustworthy than a single row silently rewritten three times. The defect was only that the reading rule was undocumented. IMPORTANT CONSEQUENCE for anyone reading gate_run: its audit_evidence split counts ROWS, not criteria — verified, since evidenced 83 + narrated 12 equals the 95 total exactly — so the headline 'narrated 12' OVERSTATES the honesty gap. Seven of those twelve are superseded Pending rows already replaced by evidenced verdicts; only five are current (AV-004, AV-075, AV-076, AV-081, AV-082) and all five are Pending, i.e. honestly not-yet-assessed. Critically, ZERO Met or Partial verdicts lack evidence, so the C7 concern that a narrated verdict is the graded party grading itself does not presently apply to any passing verdict. Deliberately NOT remedied by mutating rows: giving the stale Pending rows evidence, or rewriting them to match the current verdict, would move the metric without changing the truth, which is the failure mode this package exists to prevent.
source_span: read-only integrity audit, 2026-08-05 (operator-requested)

title: Arabic term for "Architecture" is الهيكلة — whole term family, noun-in-إضافة, definiteness preserved
decision: Rename the Arabic term for "Architecture" from الهندسة المعمارية to الهيكلة across the product, the 15 affected .dc.html design references, backend notification copy, and all asserting tests. EN keeps "Architecture" — EN/AR diverge semantically by design.
rationale: Operator decision taken on a real production login: الهندسة المعمارية reads as civil/building architecture in Arabic; الهيكلة carries the intended system-structuring sense. Scoped to the whole TERM FAMILY (معمار* in every inflection, plus standalone الهندسة), not the literal phrase, because ar.json was already inconsistent (app.committee = لجنة الهندسة المعمارية vs meetings.mom.committee = لجنة الهندسة) and a literal-only replace would have deepened that split rather than closing it. GRAMMAR: an Arabic adjective phrase (noun + agreeing adjective) becomes a genitive construct (إضافة), which requires dropping ال from the head noun — so this is a rule-based transformation, not a string substitution. DEVIATION FROM THE APPROVED PLAN: the plan collapsed both الثابت المعماري and ثابت معماري onto the definite ثابت الهيكلة; that was written without inspecting the .dc.html prose and produces ungrammatical Arabic in two shapes — after كل (لكل قرار الهيكلة: كل requires an indefinite, and قرار الهيكلة is already an إضافة) and with a trailing indefinite adjective (بثابت الهيكلة قائم, سجل قرار الهيكلة مقترح — قائم/مقترح no longer agree with a now-definite head). Definiteness is therefore PRESERVED: definite source takes الهيكلة, indefinite source takes bare هيكلة. This reproduces every example the operator approved (الهيكلة · ثوابت الهيكلة · سجل قرارات الهيكلة — all definite sources) and fixes both defects. NOT TOUCHED: مهندس/المهندسون/للمهندسين ("engineers" — same root, different word), the عمارة↔معماري word-breaker comment in DecisionSearchProvider.cs (documents SQL Server behaviour, not product copy), and docs/ + tamheed-package/ + .claude/memory/ + handoff/ (records of what happened; renaming them would falsify the record). No data migration: no HasData, no runtime seeder, zero Arabic in 96 EF migrations. VERIFIED: assert-ZERO gate over git-tracked files (not a count — git grep -c counts lines, and ar.json:2 holds two occurrences on one line); rules proven idempotent, so no rule's output can be re-matched by a later rule.

title: Every System Health tile must be backed by a real check — register the four missing ones (DEF-039)
decision: Register real server-side health checks for the four core services that currently have none (minio, keycloak, seq, hangfire), so that all six tiles in the System Health catalog reflect something actually observed. No tile may render green because nothing is looking at it.
rationale: Operator decision, 2026-08-11. The API registers only two checks (api, sqlserver) against a fixed catalog of six, so FOUR tiles were unmonitored in EVERY environment including on-prem — my original DEF-039 text wrongly said 'prod and UAT', corrected in PE-231 after reading Program.cs. A green tile that nobody checks is the un-failable check this project has now been bitten by repeatedly (see AV-117/AV-118, DEF-030/031/032, and the controls-must-detect-AND-tell pattern): the display asserted health that no probe had established. REJECTED: greying the four as 'not monitored' (honest and cheap, but leaves four core services genuinely unmonitored — it documents the gap instead of closing it) and dropping the four tiles (smallest diff, but hides the finding itself). Each new check must be proven to go RED, not merely to exist — forcing the failure is the only evidence that the tile is wired to the probe.

title: Voting eligibility may be set by EITHER Chairman or Administrator, with an attributed audit event on every change (DEF-041)
decision: The voting-eligibility toggle becomes reachable in the UI and settable by both the Chairman and the Administrator. Every change writes an attributed, hash-chained audit event recording who changed whose eligibility, from what to what, and when.
rationale: Operator decision, 2026-08-11, taken with the separation-of-duties trade-off stated explicitly. Eligibility currently cannot be changed from the UI at all — the toggle is absent from the accessibility tree — so the electorate is unmanageable. RECORDED CAVEAT, accepted by the operator: this is DETECTION, not PREVENTION. Because the Administrator can both create accounts and set eligibility, a single actor can in principle enlarge the electorate before a vote; the audit event makes that visible after the fact but does not stop it. The rejected Chairman-only options would have prevented it structurally by splitting 'who has an account' from 'who may vote'. If a future audit or an external reviewer objects to that concentration, this is the row to revisit — supersede with a new ADR rather than silently narrowing the authorization. The audit event is the load-bearing half of this decision and must be tested by asserting the row is written on a real change, not by asserting the handler was called.

title: /session (جلستي) is the GUEST/PRESENTER surface, has a full design reference, and is built to it — supersedes DEC-036
decision: Build /session to the existing GUEST / PRESENTER SHELL reference (ACMP Navigation & IA.dc.html lines 304-347), in full: expiry banner, topic card, agenda-slot card, and 'Materials for your slot'. Guest access EXPIRES AND IS ENFORCED SERVER-SIDE — the API refuses a Guest after their meeting ends and the banner reads the same value the server enforces. Guests are invited BY THE SECRETARY FROM THE MEETING SCREEN. The route is restricted to Guest plus Chairman/Secretary (preview), enforced at the API and not only by the route guard. An FR + AC must still be recorded before code (the surviving half of DEC-036).
rationale: Operator decisions, 2026-08-11, taken by interview after the factual corrections below. CORRECTS DEC-036, which called the page 'member-facing', said nothing linked to it, and recorded its content as unspecified. All three are wrong: navModel.ts sets ACCESS.session = { guest: 'full' } and FR-024 hides an area's nav item from any role lacking access, so the page is GUEST-facing and already linked for guests — the 'nothing links to it' claim came from walking the live app as an Administrator, for whom hiding it is CORRECT behaviour. A complete bilingual reference exists and fixes layout, copy and the read-only stance ('Presenter access — read-only, and expires after the meeting' / 'Presenter · Read-only'), the topic card (key, title, alt-language title, summary), the slot card (meeting name, MTG key, 'Item 3 of 6', a 15-minute time box) and the materials list (deck + diagram, each openable). FOUR THINGS THE DESIGN COULD NOT DECIDE, now decided: (1) EXPIRY IS REAL, NOT COSMETIC. The design promises expiry but NO expiry mechanism exists in code — only Delegation auto-expires. Since the page shows unpublished topic material to an EXTERNAL person, a promise the server does not keep is an exposure, not a cosmetic gap; the operator chose server-side enforcement, one source of truth for banner and API. (2) THE SECRETARY INVITES, from the meeting screen, because the Secretary schedules the meeting and knows who presents. ⚠ CONSEQUENCE THE OPERATOR SHOULD SEE: this requires the application to CREATE Keycloak users, which it has NEVER done — zero callers of the Keycloak admin API exist in src/. DEC-033 already requires a Keycloak admin READ and its own rationale says it 'must stay a read — it must not become a second write path'. That constraint is now overtaken: the two decisions share one client and it becomes read AND write. THE DEC-033 ADR MUST COVER BOTH, and must be raised before either is implemented. It must also decide where guest expiry is stored (a Keycloak user attribute vs an ACMP-side record) since the server enforces it. (3) v1 BUILDS THE FULL SHELL INCLUDING MATERIALS — a presenter without their deck cannot prepare, and the presigned-download path already exists from P13. (4) ROUTE OPENS TO GUEST + CHAIRMAN/SECRETARY so the Secretary can preview what a presenter sees; the operator accepted that this widens the audience and adds a second code path to keep correct. Today /session sits inside ProtectedRoute with NO RequireRole at all, so any signed-in user reaches it — harmless while it is a placeholder, not once it renders topic material. NOTE: Guest (realm role) is NOT Presenter (a per-topic relationship) — realm-export.json says so explicitly; do not conflate them, and do not rename the role to 'Guest/Presenter' because the claim mapper takes the leaf after the last '/'.

title: In-app user management: Administrator AND Secretary invite users and assign roles from ACMP — supersedes DEC-033 and deviates from the design's read-only-roles note
decision: Build in-app user management. Administrator and Secretary may both (a) INVITE a user — email + full name only, per the design's §(8) USER DETAIL + INVITE — which provisions the Keycloak account and surfaces a temporary password SHOWN ONCE on screen, and (b) ASSIGN ROLES from the app. Four guards are mandatory: nobody may change their own roles; granting Administrator or Chairman is a separate explicitly-confirmed step; the committee may never be left with zero Administrators; every change writes an attributed hash-chained audit event. Any role change FORCES SIGN-OUT so it takes effect immediately rather than at token expiry. ONE ADR covers this, DEC-037's guest invite, and where guest expiry is stored — same client, same credential, same audit path. ADR + FR + AC before any code.
rationale: Operator feature request and interview, 2026-08-11. THE DESIGN ALREADY SPECIFIES MOST OF IT and was found before planning: ACMP Administration.dc.html §(8) fixes the two invite fields (email, full name), the primary action, and — decisively — a status vocabulary that ALREADY CONTAINS `invited` (uStatus: active/invited/disabled). That means the roster was ALWAYS meant to show people who have not signed in yet, so DEF-038 is not a new idea but an unbuilt part of the design. ⚠ DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM THE REFERENCE, recorded rather than silent (INV-014): the design note reads 'An invitation provisions the account in Keycloak; the role is assigned there and synced read-only.' The operator has decided roles are assigned IN THE APP. That note was doing real security work — an app that cannot write roles cannot escalate privilege, so the design removed that risk BY CONSTRUCTION. The four guards replace it. SUPERSEDES DEC-033: its premise was a Keycloak admin READ to discover invited-but-never-signed-in accounts. Once the app CREATES the accounts it owns the invite record, so the roster's `invited` rows come from ACMP's own data and the read dependency disappears. Known gap accepted: accounts created directly in Keycloak — including the 26 existing production members — remain invisible until first login. CREDENTIAL DELIVERY is a temporary password shown ONCE on screen, because 'no email in v1' is a hard constraint while the design's button says 'Send invitation'; it must never be stored, logged or written to a file — the make-roster-passwords.sh CSV of 26 temp passwords is exactly the hazard this must not repeat. ⚠ RESIDUAL RISK, RAISED ONCE AND ACCEPTED BY THE OPERATOR, recorded so it stays reviewable rather than re-argued: with the Secretary able to both invite AND assign, ONE PERSON can go from nothing to a working privileged account alone. Guard 1 blocks self-escalation but not granting Administrator to a second account they created; guard 2 is a speed bump; GUARD 4 IS THE ACTUAL CONTROL AND IT IS DETECTION, NOT PREVENTION — the same shape the operator accepted in DEC-035. Revisit via a superseding ADR if a reviewer objects; never narrow it silently. ARCHITECTURE NOTE for the ADR: creating a Keycloak user AND a local member row is a distributed write, and DEF-029 means a member row can never be deleted, so a failed second write orphans permanently. Prefer writing Keycloak + a lightweight invite record and leaving ProvisionCurrentUser (ADR-0004, JIT from claims) to create the member row on first login unchanged — one creation path, ADR-0004 intact. The service account must be scoped to manage-users plus role-mapping, NEVER realm-admin, with a file-backed secret per ADR-0032.

title: UAT's database is NEVER reset; the e2e suite stays hardened against accumulated data
decision: UAT keeps its accumulated history. The Playwright suite is not given a clean database before runs; instead it remains hardened so that every spec locates its own fixtures and asserts nothing that depends on being the only rows present. This is the standing policy for any future spec.
rationale: Operator decision, 2026-08-11, taken after DEF-045. A hardened suite passes on ANY database — at 75 topics or 7,500 — whereas resetting only restarts the ratchet and RESTORES THE BLIND SPOT that hid six failures for months. The blind spot is structural, not incidental: CI rebuilds its database every run, so it cannot see this class of defect at all, and a reset-before-run UAT would have exactly the same hole. Keeping UAT accumulated is also the only way it resembles a long-lived production system, which is the specific thing UAT exists to test. REJECTED: reset-before-each-run (fast and predictable, but makes UAT stop resembling production and re-hides the class); and cleaning up the DEF-029 orphan member rows (cosmetic only — DEF-029 means they can be disabled but never deleted, and the hardened lookup no longer cares how many rows exist). CONSEQUENCE ACCEPTED: UAT will keep growing, so any NEW spec must be written page-aware and count-agnostic from the start; the four shapes to avoid are recorded in DEF-045 — non-unique identity lookups, unfiltered paginated lists, absolute counts of anything the environment can add to, and reliance on an e2e-only environment override without a keyed skip.

title: Operator approval of ADR-0040, with the guest window widened to ScheduledEnd + 24 hours and the /session alt-language title omitted
decision: Three operator answers taken 2026-08-12, before any FR-159 code was written. (1) ADR-0040 is APPROVED IN FULL - all three decisions, including decision 3, which therefore ships in the SAME pull request as the invite writer rather than following it. (2) THE GUEST ACCESS WINDOW IS ScheduledEnd + 24 HOURS, not ScheduledEnd exactly. This OVERRULES the ADR's own recommendation and the ADR text was amended rather than left to drift. (3) The /session alt-language topic title is OMITTED and the divergence recorded as a scope change (SC-006), rather than building bilingual topic titles.
rationale: ON THE WINDOW, which is the answer that changed: the ADR recommended ScheduledEnd exactly on the grounds that HasExpired is already exclusive and the phrase is 'expires after the meeting'. The operator took the wider option after the ADR stated the cost plainly - refusal is per-request and IMMEDIATE, so a meeting that overruns hands the presenter a 401 in the middle of presenting. A committee meeting running past its scheduled end is ordinary, not exceptional, and a governance tool that cuts off the person currently speaking is a worse failure than 24 more hours of scoped read access. The 24-hour choice also covers same-day follow-up: a presenter asked to send something after the session can still reach their own material. WHAT IT COSTS, recorded so it is never a surprise: an external person holds read access to their slot's unpublished topic material for a day after the meeting. That is bounded (one slot, read-only, still enforced per request and still swept into a disabled Keycloak account), and it is the operator's call to make - AC-092 requires that expiry be REAL and SERVER-ENFORCED, which it remains; it does not fix the duration. Nothing else in ADR-0040 moves: the boundary stays exclusive, stays a single stored column read by all three readers, and stays computed at invite time. ON THE ALT TITLE: OQ-073's recommendation was accepted - a migration, two form changes, bilingual validation and a backfill for every existing topic is a bilingual-content FR, not a line of chrome on the guest shell.

title: Operator disposition of the four open items after FR-159: OQ-069 (Users moves out of Administration), OQ-071 (split the grant proof), DEF-050 (verify SSM, then fix per ADR-0032), DW-025 (guest windows follow the meeting)
decision: Four answers taken 2026-08-12 by interview, after FR-159 closed. (1) OQ-069 - THE USERS SURFACE MOVES OUT OF ADMINISTRATION. A new Members area holds the directory, the invite (FR-156) and role assignment (FR-157), reachable by Administrator AND Secretary; the Administration area keeps system health, roles, job monitor, streams and notification settings and stays Administrator-only. The Users tab is REMOVED from Administration rather than duplicated - one surface, one place for authorization to be right. (2) OQ-071 - SPLIT THE OBLIGATION. The minimum-grant proof becomes an automated LOCAL test against the bundled Keycloak, asserting that a narrower grant is REFUSED and that manage-users succeeds, so it re-runs every CI run; UAT keeps a reduced CONNECTIVITY check that the service account reaches Keycloak through the deployed proxy with the SSM-delivered secret. (3) DEF-050 - VERIFY BEFORE FIXING, then fix per ADR-0032: read the DEPLOYED env on prod and UAT to settle whether a real Webex token is actually interpolated (which decides the severity the row could not), then mount the five Webex secrets as compose secrets on api and worker, make gen-secrets write them UNCONDITIONALLY, and drop the environment entries. (4) DW-025 - GUEST WINDOWS FOLLOW THE MEETING, and wider than the row proposed: rescheduling MOVES each guest's window, cancelling CLOSES it, and removing a guest from their slot CLOSES it.
rationale: ON OQ-069, the operator rejected both cheaper readings. Narrowing FR-156/157 to Administrator-only was available and refused: the requirements say 'Administrator or Secretary' and the server already honours it, so the product - not the requirement - was wrong. Per-tab gating inside /admin was also refused because it still puts the Secretary inside the Administration area, which is the exact thing the question flagged (SoD-5, permission-matrix row 27). Moving the surface out is the only option where the capability genuinely leaves that area AND does not exist twice. The cost is accepted: the Administration reference draws a Users tab and the design's nav matrix has no Members area, so this is an INV-014 divergence, recorded as SC-008 rather than made silently. ON OQ-071, the substance of the obligation is that a stub cannot evaluate Keycloak's own authorization - and that substance is satisfiable against the same image and the same realm export locally, where it can run on EVERY CI run instead of once on a box that is stopped when idle. What UAT uniquely adds is deployment topology (the /kc prefix behind nginx, the SSM-delivered secret), which is a connectivity question, so it keeps a connectivity check. A one-off manual proof on a stopped box decays; an automated one does not. ON DEF-050, the row itself admitted an unverified fact - 'exposure is probably nil' was inferred from the .env EXAMPLES while the deployed environment comes from SSM. Verifying first is the difference between fixing a dead artifact and rotating a live credential, and this project has paid for asserting instead of checking before. The fix direction follows ADR-0032 because the ADR is explicit and the alternative (accepting environment delivery) would need its own deviation record for a Phase-2 integration that is currently off. ⚠ THE FIX HAS A TRAP THE OPERATOR WAS SHOWN: a compose secrets: entry whose file is missing fails the WHOLE STACK, and gen-secrets only writes the Webex files when WEBEX_ENABLED=true - so the writes must become unconditional, exactly the treatment KeycloakAdmin__ClientSecret got in DW-024. ON DW-025, the operator overruled the deferral AND widened it. The reasoning that made deferral defensible was that the failure mode is inconvenience rather than exposure - but that is only true of RESCHEDULE. Cancelling a meeting leaves an external person holding live access to unpublished material for a meeting that will not happen, and un-assigning a guest from their slot leaves access to a topic they are no longer presenting; both are exposure, not inconvenience. Once the write path exists for one caller, the other two are the same call.

title: Operator disposition of the four decisions blocking the remaining Partials: DEF-057 (implement stream scope), AC-009 vs AC-034 (AC-034 wins), DEF-056 (audit policy-layer denials), AC-011 (turn the ADR-0038 flag on in CI's e2e stack)
decision: FOUR ANSWERS TAKEN 2026-08-13 BY INTERVIEW, after Tranches A-C established what was actually blocking each remaining Partial. Recorded BEFORE the work, because three of the four are unbuilt and a decision living only in a conversation is one the next session re-asks. (1) DEF-057 - IMPLEMENT STREAM SCOPE PROPERLY, do not drop it. The control is specified in permission-role-matrix section E.1, is registered in DI, is unit-tested, and appears in NO POLICY - so it is never evaluated and FAILS OPEN. The operator chose to make it real rather than remove it from the matrix. ⚠ THE PLAN IS THREE STEPS, NOT FOUR, and the reduction is a measured fact rather than an optimisation: production has ZERO topics, so there is no existing free-text stream data to reconcile against Stream.Code. Remaining: seed the committee's real streams, assign members to them, then wire StreamScopeRequirement into the stream-bounded write policies. ⚠ THE ORDER IS NOT NEGOTIABLE - wiring before seeding takes the system from fails-open straight to REFUSING EVERY stream-bounded write, because Topic.cs:104 requires at least one affected stream to submit so no topic is ever unscoped, and no member holds a stream. ⚠ BLOCKED ON THE OPERATOR: the stream names AND the member-to-stream assignments. The operator undertook to supply them and has not yet; I will not invent a taxonomy for a governance system, and seeding streams while leaving members unassigned is the same outage in slower motion. (2) AC-009 vs AC-034 - AC-034 WINS, AND THE CODE ALREADY AGREES. The two approved ACs contradict each other: ownership is granted ON Accept, so an Owner exists only post-Accept, and AC-034 says only the Secretary may edit after Acceptance while AC-009 says the Owner's edit is accepted. The operator chose the conservative reading - once Accepted, a topic is committee property and its content is locked; the Owner keeps their other capabilities but not editing. NO CODE CHANGES: AC-009 is narrowed to its refusal clause (recorded as SC-009), which #253 already proved live. (3) DEF-056 - ADD AN IAuthorizationMiddlewareResultHandler that emits the audit event when the policy layer forbids. One seam covering every endpoint including ones added later - the same deny-by-default reasoning DEF-052 used, because an opt-in list silently exempts whatever route is added next. ⚠ Two implementation constraints established with the advisor: recover the failing policy name from policy.Requirements (CapabilityRequirement carries PolicyName - confirm there is exactly one and not a merged set), and emit ONLY on authorizeResult.Forbidden, never on Challenged (the 401 path, already covered) and never on success. Resolve the sink from context.RequestServices. Rejected: amending AC-006 to drop the audit clause, on the grounds that 'who tried to mutate governance data and was refused' is precisely the question an architecture committee's log gets asked. (4) AC-011 - TURN KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_ENABLED ON IN CI's E2E STACK. This does far more than unblock one AC: the entire ADR-0038 write path (invite, role assignment, forced sign-out, guest disable) is registered only when the flag is on, so today CI runs seven services with a real Keycloak and never constructs IIdentityProvider at all - the path is reachable only by the manual UAT probe. ✓ VERIFIED BEFORE COMMITTING TO IT: deploy/docker-compose.yml (the dev/e2e compose, not the cloud one) already mounts KeycloakAdmin__ClientSecret into keycloak-config, api and worker at lines 163/183/338 and declares the secret file at 433, so ValidateOnStart will not stop the hosts and a missing secrets file will not fail the stack. Remaining choice at implementation time: set the flag in e2e.yml's env (CI only) or in deploy/.env.example (which changes dev too) - prefer the narrower unless dev should match.

title: Operator disposition of DEF-100: NFR-019 is KEPT as written and internal-network plaintext becomes tracked work, not an accepted boundary
decision: The operator was offered four dispositions for DEF-100 and chose to KEEP NFR-019 unchanged. No scope change is made. The requirement continues to mandate TLS 1.2 or higher on application-to-SQL-Server, application-to-Tarseem and application-to-Keycloak communication, and the fact that the Keycloak and api hops run plaintext HTTP on the Docker network becomes tracked work under DW-074 rather than a boundary the register accepts. THE THREE REJECTED OPTIONS, recorded because the rejection carries the meaning: narrowing NFR-019 to the public endpoint plus the database hop and naming the private Docker network as an accepted boundary - which would have extended OQ-024's mTLS reasoning to ordinary TLS and closed the requirement immediately with zero work; narrowing it further to exclude the SQL hop as well, on the grounds that TrustServerCertificate=True means encrypted but not authenticated; and carrying the finding undispositioned. CONSEQUENCE, STATED PLAINLY: NFR-019 remains Approved and UNVERIFIABLE, and correctly has no acceptance criterion. It cannot record Met until DW-074 lands. This is the same posture NFR-054 holds behind DW-066 - a requirement deliberately left failing rather than reworded to match what shipped.
rationale: The choice is a judgement about where ACMP's trust boundary sits, and it is the operator's to make rather than a reading of the code. The case for narrowing was real: OQ-024 already resolved that internal Compose-network services need no mTLS, the hops in question sit on a private Docker network on a single host, and the public edge is configured exactly to the floor NFR-019 states - ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3 in cloud-443.conf.template. The case for keeping it, which the operator took, is that ordinary TLS and mTLS are different questions, that OQ-024 settled only the second, and that an on-prem committee platform handling governance data should not silently downgrade a Must-priority security requirement because the current deployment happens to put everything on one host. Keeping the requirement means the register continues to state the target rather than the status quo.

title: ACTIVATE ALL TWELVE DEMAND-TRIGGERED DEFERRED-WORK ROWS. The operator is the demand channel those triggers name, and they stated the demand for every one - so by the triggers' own terms all twelve have fired.
decision:
d1 - ALL TWELVE demand-triggered deferred-work rows are ACTIVATED: DW-028 (session presenter preview), DW-032 (triage reclassify), DW-033 (configurable backlog columns, FR-032), DW-035 (audit-log export, FR-154), DW-036 (configurable retention, FR-155 / NFR-059 / NFR-060), DW-038 (PNG chart export, FR-142), DW-039 (wiki version diff, FR-117), DW-040 (drag-to-reprioritize, FR-037), DW-061 (not-optimized-for-mobile notice, NFR-063), DW-063 (configuration-driven stream taxonomy, NFR-010), DW-068 (locale-aware NUMBER formatting, NFR-037), DW-069 (the bilingual glossary, NFR-039).

d2 - THREE REQUIREMENTS RETURN FROM Deferred TO Approved in the same delta, because activated work is v1 work and leaving the requirement labelled not-in-v1 preserves a contradiction rather than resolving it: FR-032, FR-154 and FR-155. All three were part of SC-020's set of 24, which moved requirements DOWNWARD to say 'not in v1'. This moves three of them back UP. The other nine rows' requirements are already Approved or Implemented and are untouched.

d3 - DW-069 IS ACTIVATED BUT CANNOT BE COMPLETED BY THIS PROJECT'S USUAL MEANS, and that is stated here so a later session does not read Activated as buildable-to-done. Its requirement's first clause asks for a single source of canonical bilingual terms, and no such artifact exists - the two documents that each claim to be it name the other and neither contains a single Arabic character. What activation authorises is BUILDING that artifact, which is the cheapest first step its own row identifies. The second clause - no term carrying more than one Arabic rendering - remains UNDECIDABLE until the glossary exists, and adjudicating candidate divergences needs an Arabic reader. Activation does not manufacture one.

d4 - THE OPERATOR WAS SHOWN ALL TWELVE IN FULL BEFORE DECIDING, and was told in the same breath that activating all twelve is a scope event that materially expands v1. Their first answer, 'I need all', was ambiguous between 'show me all twelve' and 'activate all twelve'; it was NOT acted on. They were asked which they meant, answered 'show me all twelve in full, then I'll decide', were given the complete text of every row, and then said 'activate all twelve'. The sequence is recorded because a two-word instruction that expands v1 by twelve items should show its provenance.
rationale:
d1: eleven of the twelve were deferred on the reasoning that nobody had asked for the capability - their triggers say so almost verbatim ('when a power user asks', 'the first time a Chairman or Secretary asks', 'when an auditor first needs', 'the committee decides'). Those triggers name DEMAND as the activating condition and name no other. The operator IS the demand channel for this product, so their stating the demand is precisely the event the triggers describe; treating it as anything less would make the triggers unfireable in practice. This is the opposite of the manufactured-status move the deferred-work-reviewed advisory guards against - that failure is closing a row whose trigger never fired in order to green an advisory, whereas here the trigger fired and the row moves to Activated, which makes the advisory LARGER rather than smaller because Activated rows still count as open.

d2: this is the same reasoning applied one day earlier to FR-035 via SC-028, and it is applied here deliberately rather than being rediscovered later. A requirement reading Deferred while its deferred-work row reads Activated is a contradiction no gate or readiness rule can see, because a requirement's lifecycle_status and a deferred-work row's lifecycle_status are unrelated columns that nothing compares. Leaving three such pairs behind while fixing a fourth would be worse than not having found the pattern.

d3: recorded because the honest failure mode here is a future session seeing Activated, building an English glossary file, and calling the requirement met - which would satisfy the letter of clause one while leaving the thing the requirement exists for, a canonical ARABIC source, still absent.

d4: the ambiguity was real and the two readings led to materially different work - one a presentation, the other a twelve-row scope expansion. Guessing would have been the cheaper path and the wrong one.

SL-032 under a new PH-7 contains DW-061 (the not-optimized-for-mobile notice, NFR-063), DW-040 (drag-to-reprioritize, FR-037), DW-038 (PNG chart export, FR-142) and DW-032 (triage reclassify). DW-061 is built FIRST. The other nine activated rows stay Activated with no slice until they are scheduled: DW-028, DW-033, DW-035, DW-036, DW-039, DW-063, DW-068, DW-069 and DW-037.

d2 - DEF-087 IS FIXED FORWARD ONLY. Every wbs-item created from now on carries a slice_id, and the 155 historical items are NOT backfilled. Slice-scope wbs-done stays honestly blind for the 28 closed slices and the defect row says so rather than being closed as repaired. THE BACKFILL IS THE PART THAT WAS DECLINED, not the diagnosis.

d3 - THE v1 RELEASE CLOSE-OUT IS NOT SCHEDULED. Thirteen rows were just declared live work; running the ceremony now would close out a release over scope that was opened hours earlier. CONSEQUENCE, recorded so it is not rediscovered: the rows whose activation trigger names 'before release sign-off' - the WCAG manual pass (DW-041), the Firefox and WebKit browser matrix (DW-067), and alt-text route coverage (DW-071) - therefore do NOT fire, and stay carried.

The cost is that slice-scope readiness stays decorative for the 28 closed slices, and that cost is accepted and stated rather than papered over.

d3: closing out a release over scope opened the same day would make the close-out a ceremony rather than a check. The coupling to the accessibility and browser-matrix rows is the reason this is recorded as a decision rather than left implicit - a later session reading those three rows will see 'before release sign-off' and needs to know the sign-off was deliberately not scheduled, not merely forgotten.

Re-dating it to a date nobody has committed to would convert a true signal into a comfortable one, and a red control that everyone learns to ignore is how the next blind control gets built. ASM-017 was offered for escalation twice and declined twice; recording the decline explicitly matters more than the escalation would have, because otherwise a third session offers it a third time.

title: WBS-23.3 PNG export is built on html-to-image, not the pre-selected modern-screenshot: the spike inverted a metadata-based ranking, and the operator took the working package over the maintained one
decision:
d1 - `html-to-image` 1.11.13 IS THE DEPENDENCY. It enters `src/Acmp.Web/package.json` as a runtime dependency of the SPA and `WBS-23.3` / `DW-038` / `FR-142`'s PNG half is built on it. `modern-screenshot` 4.7.0 - the package named as the pick in the prompt library's dependency table and carried into the build session as settled - is REJECTED. It is not patched, not vendored, and not revisited.

d2 - THE SHIPPED CSP IS NOT TOUCHED. `style-src 'self'` with no `unsafe-inline` stays exactly as it is in both `deploy/nginx/default.conf.template` and `deploy/nginx/cloud-443.conf.template`. The spike established that the DOM-to-image technique does not need `unsafe-inline` at all, so `DW-022`'s 2026-07-16 finding - that `style-src 'self'` ships with the code as-is - stands unmodified and was never in question.

d3 - THE ALTERNATIVES WERE PUT UP AND DECLINED. Patching or vendoring `modern-screenshot` for its one unguarded property read was declined; hand-rolling the pipeline with no dependency was declined; and deferring `DW-038` back out of `SL-032` on the grounds that the price rose from 'a canvas draw and a download' to 'a runtime dependency' was declined. `WBS-23.3` therefore stays in `SL-032` in `DEC-068` d1's order, and no scope-change row is needed because the requirement, the slice and the work item are all unchanged - only the means.
rationale:
d1: the ranking that produced the original pick was built entirely on package-registry metadata - unpacked size, runtime dependency count, weekly downloads, last-published date - and every number in it was correct. Measured against the only axis that decides anything here, whether the thing runs under this application's Content-Security-Policy, the ranking inverts completely: `modern-screenshot` throws on every card in both locales because `embedWebFont` appends a style element to a scratch document that inherits the page's CSP and then dereferences the resulting null sheet, and `html-to-image` - rejected in that table as the largest and stalest candidate - works with fonts embedded and contributes not one violation. The full run is `PE-578`. The known cost of this choice is stated rather than discovered later: `html-to-image` was last published 2025-04-19 and is materially older than the alternative, but it declares ZERO runtime dependencies, so an unmaintained upstream here means no new fixes rather than an accumulating transitive advisory surface, and the failure mode of the alternative is total.

d2: nothing in the spike produced a reason to widen a security header, which was the outcome the prompt library explicitly told the session to STOP and ask about. Recording that the condition never arose matters as much as recording the choice, because the next session reading `DW-038`'s brief will find the prediction that inline styles in an SVG foreignObject would be blocked, and that prediction is simply false - a parent document's `style-src` does not reach inside an SVG rendered as an image.

d3: `font: false` is recorded as declined-by-implication rather than untried. It is the only configuration in which the rejected package does not crash, and it silently breaks the Arabic layout - the card title reflows into its own subtitle because that library omits width and height from the styles it copies. An escape route that produces a correct English PNG and a broken Arabic one in a bilingual product is worse than a crash, because a crash is visible.

title: Triage-time reclassification gets its OWN requirement row (FR-164) via a scope change, rather than being bound to FR-029 or shipped with an unbound acceptance criterion
decision:
d1 - A NEW REQUIREMENT ROW, FR-164, IS CREATED BY SC-031 and AC-143 binds to it. The capability shipped by WBS-23.4 - a Secretary or Chairman correcting a topic's type and source before Acceptance - had NO requirement anywhere in the register. The DEF-086 precedent governs: a shipped capability with no requirement row got FR-163, and this follows it.

d2 - BINDING THE CRITERION TO FR-029 WAS REJECTED. FR-029 covers moving a topic into Triage, 'reviewing its fields', and then accepting, rejecting or deferring it. Reclassification is arguably within its spirit, but its letter says nothing about changing type or source, and FR-029 is already Implemented - so binding here would have made an Implemented requirement silently carry a clause nobody wrote into it.

d3 - SHIPPING WITH AN UNBOUND CRITERION WAS REJECTED. The store permits it and nine criteria already have no requirement_id, but every one of those is infrastructure - TLS, ECR publishing, budget alarms, memory budgets - and no FEATURE criterion is unbound. An unbound feature criterion is the invisible-gap shape DEF-089 and DW-038 exist to close.

title: DW-082 is closed by writing the missing handler tests before #307 merges; ALL FOUR activated streams are in scope; the leaked vite processes are killed and the gap that let them leak is filed; three of this session's findings become lesson rows
decision:
d1 - DW-082 IS CLOSED BY WRITING THE MISSING TESTS, NOT BY MOVING THE THRESHOLD OR REFUSING THE UPGRADE. The experiment settled that coverage-v8 v4 is the honest counter: on ErrorBoundary.tsx, both providers record the SAME uncalled inline onClick on line 30, and they differ only in where they count it - v3 has no zero-hit statements so the line is credited, v4 records statement 3 at zero hits and that propagates into the line metric. Since ADR-0016's gate is lines only, v3 renders every untested inline handler invisible to it. The twenty files were never properly covered. So the route is: identify each affected file's uncovered lines the same way the experiment did, write tests that actually invoke those handlers, and merge #307 once the gate passes honestly. THIS IS THE ONLY ROUTE THAT ENDS WITH BOTH A CURRENT vitest AND A TRUE 95%. #307, #261 and #137 stay open until it does; #307 supersedes the other two in content and closing it would lose the paired bump.

d2 - ALL FOUR ACTIVATED STREAMS ARE IN SCOPE. The operator's answer to 'what runs next' was ALL: the DW-082 handler tests, SL-033 beginning at WBS-24.1, DW-080 (the .NET 8-to-10 migration carrying DW-066's alpine move), and DW-079 (the NFR-018 ASVS evidence pack). NOTHING IS DESELECTED. ⚠ THE ORDER IS NOT SETTLED BY THAT ANSWER and the sequence below is the AGENT'S RECOMMENDATION, recorded as such so a later session does not read it as the operator's instruction, and freely reorderable by them: (1) the DW-082 handler tests, because SL-033 will add new components with new inline handlers and doing this first means WBS-24.1's own code lands under a gate that can see them; (2) SL-033 from WBS-24.1 in DEC-071 d1's order; (3) DW-080 ALONE with nothing else in flight, which its own row requires - it is a migration with a musl-and-globalization failure mode a unit suite cannot see; (4) DW-079, document-only and slottable anywhere.

d3 - THE SIX LEAKED vite PROCESSES ARE KILLED AND THE GAP THAT LET THEM LEAK IS FILED. Six vite dev servers plus their six npx parents, all rooted in src/Acmp.Web/node_modules on ports 5199, 5201, 5233, 5241, 4173 and 8124, the oldest thirteen days old, were holding rolldown-binding.win32-x64-msvc.node open - which is why npm ci failed on the host with EPERM and EBUSY and why an earlier npm ci gutted node_modules midway. They were re-enumerated immediately before killing rather than taken from a stale list, and nothing outside that set was touched; 65 unrelated node processes were left running. THE STRUCTURAL POINT, and it is why a row follows rather than just a kill: trap 28 covers leftover visual-verify FILES - a vr-*.tsx in src/ that would ship - and nothing covered leaked PROCESSES, which is exactly why these survived thirteen days across multiple sessions while a file-level guard ran clean.

d4 - THREE OF THIS SESSION'S FINDINGS BECOME LESSON ROWS, born Proposed. The operator selected: the instrument-changed finding, the shared-mechanism refinement of LL-009, and the base-image-versus-package-repo coupling. They are written Proposed rather than Approved because approved lessons are IMMUTABLE in this store and the operator has chosen the findings but not yet read the final wording; confirming the text is a separate, deliberate act. The fourth candidate - that a discovery guard converts a broken instrument's silent false-pass into a loud false-fail - was NOT selected and is not filed; it restates trap 31 with new evidence rather than adding a rule.
rationale:
d1: the experiment inverted the row's own framing, which is why it was worth running. The twenty red files looked like a regression caused by a tool change; they are a pre-existing gap the old tool concealed. Lowering the threshold was already forbidden and is now more so - the number would be hiding real untested code rather than an artefact. Refusing the upgrade on the grounds that v4 miscounts is no longer supportable.

d2: recording 'all' as scope while marking the order as the agent's keeps two things separate that are easy to conflate - what the operator decided, and what the agent inferred about how to do it. DEC-071 d3 set the precedent that an operator's container choice is recorded as theirs and the agent's disagreement recorded as the agent's; this is the same discipline applied to sequencing rather than to slicing.

d3: the kill is trivially reversible and the row is the durable half. A cleanup that is not part of the loop that creates the mess will not happen; that is the same reasoning that put the base-image coupling note into the Dockerfile rather than only into a register row.

d4: immutability is the whole reason for Proposed. LL-011's own history shows what a lesson costs when its wording has to be superseded rather than edited, and the operator selecting a finding is not the same as approving a sentence.

title: OPERATOR INTERVIEW, 2026-08-25 (SECOND ROUND): DEF-108 CARRIED OPEN AT HIGH SEVERITY WITH READINESS FALSE; `scripts/**` CARVED OUT OF THE DIRECT-TO-MAIN RULE *AND* A POST-PUSH CI CHECK MANDATED; EVERY RED FROM THE FTS TEST IS REAL; A CONTAINER-STARTUP TIMEOUT GOES IN FIRST, BEFORE WBS-24.1
decision:
d1 - DEF-108 IS CARRIED **OPEN AT HIGH SEVERITY**, with a recurrence trigger, and `readiness_check` therefore returns **ready:FALSE** until it is chased. **THIS OVERRODE THE AGENT'S RECOMMENDATION**, which was to convert it to a deferred-work row so readiness could return TRUE. The operator chose the strictest available option and the blocking consequence is accepted deliberately, not overlooked: nothing may be declared done at package scope while it stands.

d2 - THE BRANCHING RULE IS AMENDED IN **BOTH** DIRECTIONS, which was also stricter than either single option offered. (a) STRUCTURAL: anything touching `scripts/**` goes branch -> PR -> green CI -> squash-merge, like any other code. It is no longer covered by the direct-to-main allowance. (b) DISCIPLINARY: after **ANY** direct push to `main`, CI is polled to completion - `status` until `completed`, then `conclusion` - regardless of what the commit touched. ⚠ Adding `scripts/**` to the workflows' path-ignore was explicitly REJECTED and must not be proposed again: several `scripts/*.mjs` ARE the CI gates (check-coverage, check-i18n, check-vulns, check-hardcoded-strings), so ignoring that path would mean a change to a gate never runs the gate.

d3 - A RED FROM `SearchProvidersFtsTests` IS TREATED AS **REAL**: stop and investigate. Re-running to see whether it passes is NOT the response. **ALSO STRICTER THAN THE AGENT'S RECOMMENDATION**, which was to re-run once and log the occurrence. The reasoning the operator's choice rests on is in the register already: that test is the ONLY place any FREETEXT branch executes against real SQL Server, so it is the single test whose silent loss would be least visible and most expensive.

d4 - A CONTAINER-STARTUP TIMEOUT IS ADDED INSIDE THE TEST so a hung container fails fast with a legible message instead of burning the backend job's 25-minute ceiling and reporting 'cancelled' - a verdict that is neither pass nor fail and reads like a fluke.
